method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation No. 104, compilation date 4 June 2026 (includes amendments to Act No. 75, 2025; register id C2026C00227), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03712.txt (retrieved 13 October 2026). Not deposited: Privacy Regulation 2013; Privacy (Credit Reporting) Code 2014 (the prescribed default amount is an input)

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the individual whose personal information is held: whether the holder is bound (s 6 APP entity; s 6C; s 6D small business operator and the $3,000,000 turnover test, inclusive, with s 6D(4)(a) once-above-always-above; s 6EA opt-in; s 7B(3) employee records); APP 12 access (duty, the 30-day and reasonable-period deadlines, charges, refusal notice); APP 13 correction (duty, associated statement, no charge); APP 7 direct marketing (7.2-7.5 exceptions, 7.7 opt-out, 7.8 the Do Not Call Register Act and Spam Act as inputs); Part IIIA as the lives need it: s 6N credit information, s 21C naming the bureau, s 21P refusal notice, s 6Q default information ($150 or a prescribed higher amount as input), s 21D listing conditions (14 days after notice, nothing before 18), s 20W retention table, s 20X items 4 and 5 debt agreements, s 20V(2), s 20R access (10 days, free once in 3 months), s 20T correction (30 days), s 20K ban period; Part IIIC ss 26WE, 26WF, 26WH, 26WK, 26WL (eligible data breach; serious harm as an input; whether and how I must be told); Part V ss 36, 40(1)-(1B), 41(1)(c) (whether the Commissioner will investigate). Not encoded: APPs 1-6 and 8-11; s 6E; the s 6DA(2) formula (missing from the deposit); the rest of Part IIIA; Part IIIC exceptions and directions; representative complaints, conciliation, determinations, penalties; Schedule 2 statutory tort.
seat: the individual whose personal information is held (the borrower, the debtor, the customer, the user whose data is breached)
